descripcion: At B1 you compare two things using comparative and superlative adjectives, plus simple connectors like but. The finer, weighted contrast used at higher levels comes later — clear comparatives and a stated preference are enough here.

filas: This one is cheaper than that one.

ejemplos.texto: This phone is cheaper than that one.
It's the best option, in my opinion.
They're quite similar, but this one is faster.

notas: Short adjectives take -er/-est (cheaper, cheapest); longer ones take more/most (more expensive).
Than is needed after a comparative: cheaper than, not just cheaper.
The is needed before a superlative: the best, the cheapest.

contraste.es: Spanish compares with más… que, while English uses -er and -est for short adjectives (bigger, the biggest). The typical errors are more big and more bigger.
contraste.de: German uses the same endings (größer, am größten), so -er and -est feel natural. The trap is long adjectives: German teurer becomes expensiver, where English says more expensive.
contraste.it: Italian compares with più (più grande), which leads to more big instead of bigger. English uses -er and -est for short adjectives and more only for longer ones.
contraste.fr: French compares with plus (plus grand), which leads to more big instead of bigger. English uses -er and -est for short adjectives and more only for longer ones.
contraste.pt: Portuguese compares with mais (mais alto), which leads to more tall instead of taller. English uses -er and -est for short adjectives and more only for longer ones.

errores: Using more with a short adjective that should take -er.
autochequeo: Is than used after every comparative?
Is the used before every superlative?
Are short and long adjectives formed correctly (-er/-est vs. more/most)?
Have I stated a clear preference?
Have I used more than one form?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on comparatives and superlatives. Check than, the, and whether short or long adjective forms are used correctly throughout the comparison. Do not rewrite the text.

es: *el más alto de la clase* rendered with *of*: *the tallest of the class* instead of *the tallest in the class*.
de: *so groß wie* rendered as *so tall like* instead of *as tall as*.
it: *il più alto della classe* rendered with *of*: *the tallest of the class* instead of *the tallest in the class*.
fr: *le plus grand de la classe* rendered with *of*: *the tallest of the class* instead of *the tallest in the class*.
pt: *o mais alto da turma* rendered with *of*: *the tallest of the class* instead of *the tallest in the class*.
